newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sixty Japanese believed held hostage in Peru.
newsitem.headline: Sixty Japanese believed held hostage in Peru.

text.p: About 60 Japanese are among the estimated 200 hostages being held in the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima, Peru, by leftist guerrillas, Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda told a news conference on Wednesday.

"At the moment we believe that there are about 60 (Japanese), including embassy employees," Ikeda said. "Three of the 20 embassy employees who were being held hostage have been freed and there may be slightly more than 40 Japanese working for Japanese companies still being held."

However, Ikeda added that concern over the safety of the hostages made it impossible to disclose the names of the individuals or companies whose executives were being held by guerrillas from the Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA).
MRTA rebels late on Tuesday fired a rocket and sprayed bullets into Ambassador Morihisa Aoki's residence before storming the building during a reception to honour the Japanese Emperor's birthday.
The rebels have threatened to kill the hostages, including high-ranking foreign diplomats, unless the Peruvian government freed jailed comrades.

Japan's NHK public broadcasting network reported that executives from the Lima branches of Toyota Motor Corp, NEC Corp, Asahi Chemical Industry Co, Matsushita Electric Industrial Co and Mitsui Mining and Smelting Co, were among the hostages.
Kyodo news agency said businessmen from trading firms Marubeni Corp and Mitsui & Co Ltd were also among those held prisoner.
